meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-library-28). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

notes.Breakdown.FundSol.integrable_kernelSecon: The source must vanish at the evaluation point. This cancellation makes the Hessian-kernel expression an ordinary integrable function.
notes.Breakdown.FundSol.kernel: Lean gives inverse zero a total value. The smoothness and differential kernel identities are proved away from the origin.
notes.Breakdown.FundSol.secondPartial_potentia: The vanishing-source hypothesis is part of this pointwise formula and must be retained when using it.
notes.Breakdown.GradientBoundedOn: The name mentions the gradient, but the predicate also bounds the velocity itself by the same constant on the closed interval.
notes.Breakdown.NoBoundedSmoothSolution: The excluded solution has one energy bound for the entire time domain. A bound on each shorter interval alone does not supply that hypothesis.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.IsSolenoidalSymbol: This predicate includes conjugate symmetry, which ensures a real physical field, as well as the frequency-divergence condition.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.pressureSymbol: The formula uses total complex division at zero frequency. The later identification with the bilinear pressure symbol is stated almost everywhere.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.toL2C: This conversion returns zero when the input does not belong to L2. Its representative identities assume L2 membership.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.toWeightL1: This conversion is a total function with a zero fallback outside weighted L1. The subsequent representation lemmas assume the required L1 membership.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.ContinuousVarConst: Continuity is asserted on the interval beginning at the chosen initial time, including that initial endpoint and excluding the terminal endpoint.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.PairingDilate: This definition is an implication from the velocity-pairing interface. Its named discharge proves that entire implication.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.SliceIntegrand: The interface retains the velocity-pairing and advection-by-parts premises used to identify the weak integrand.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.SliceMeasurable: The velocity-pairing interface is an explicit antecedent of this measurability interface.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.TrilinearDilate: This definition is an implication from the weak-gradient interface. Its named discharge retains that premise.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.VarConstGood: The interface assumes both bilinear integrability and the scalar variation-of-constants identity.
notes.Breakdown.WeakProfile.VarConstInner: The interface assumes bilinear integrability and uses a strictly positive heat regularization parameter.
notes.Breakdown.eq_of_isSolutionOn: Both solutions have bounded energy on the comparison interval. The velocity-and-gradient bound is required for the designated comparison solution.
notes.Breakdown.tendsto_integral_pressureDefec: The averaging radius tends to infinity in this argument. These mollifiers are used to average over larger regions.
